text: player
Hinata Takanashi
The sea looks absolutely stunning...
Beach, One Han City
Natsuki Shinomiya
Ah-ha! First one here!
Hideki Akechi
Looks like we've got this entire beach all to ourselves.
Mirai
I mean, it's not really beach season yet, is it?
But the sun feels so perfect today!
Definitely! Plenty of sunlight without the scorching heat.
Hey, you slowpokes! Don't leave me hanging out here by myself! Catch up already!
Since a few friends had some free time lately, I thought it'd be fun to get everyone to the beach.
The water's too chilly for swimming right now, but that hasn't stopped everyone from having fun.
Especially Hinata and Mirai, who are running around like excited kids.
Yui Yagi
Watching the others play from afar, Yui narrows her eyes slightly, as if the sun is too bright for her.
Though we've been talking a lot recently, this is my first time inviting her out. I still can't quite figure out what's going on in her mind...
Everyone seems to be enjoying themselves.
Yes, they are. Are you enjoying yourself too?
I don't know.
Yui neither confirms nor denies... better to steer the conversation elsewhere.
Speaking of beaches, when was the last time you visited one?
10 years and 3 months ago.
That's quite a long time...
Wait, you remember it down to the month?
Yes, it was the first time I went to the beach with my family.
I didn't know how to swim then, which was disappointing, so I took swimming lessons afterward.
Oh? So you can swim now?
Are you doubting me?
No, not at all! I'd never do that.
That said, I'm having a hard time imagining Yui in the water.
I'd love to prove it to you, but the ocean's still off-limits for swimming.
What a pity.
How about we go beachcombing instead?
It's okay, searching for seashells on the beach is fun too.
Hearing this, Yui suddenly turns her gaze toward me.
Wh-what's wrong?
Senpai...
If I find any pretty shells, I'll give them to you.
Sure, thank you.
Sure, I'll try to find some nice ones too.
Hey! How about a game of beach volleyball?!
Hehehe... I knew someone would suggest this. Look! I came prepared with a ball!
Ah, this must be the work of some divine power... the god of spheres has blessed me with its power!
I mean, people typically bring volleyballs to the beach anyway...
It does sound fun, though. Are you and {var:player_nickname} joining us, Yui?
Of course, I'd never turn down a game.
Next to me, Yui nods slightly, her face as unreadable as always.
After drawing lots to form teams, I'm grouped with Yui and Hideki.
I assumed Yui wouldn't be athletic, but she's surprisingly skilled at volleyball.
But none of us has had any professional training, so the match basically looks like a bunch of amateurs just fumbling around...
Here it comes!
Hmph!
Take this!
Haha, it's nice to get some exercise once in a while.
Mmm, this is fun.
Nice one! We just scored!
The game has been neck and neck, and now we're at 20-19, our match point.
Nooo... we can't afford to lose this one!
I'm going all out! Take this! Midnight Inferno!
Big talk, slow walk. I jumped the gun trying to block that slowpoke...
{var:player_nickname}! Catch it!
The volleyball soars toward my head.
I track the ball while checking my teammates' positions from the corner of my eye. Yui is standing back, and she seems to be looking at me.
Somehow I can feel the confidence in her eyes. But...
A quick look at the other side shows all three opponents standing deep in their court, with the net area completely unguarded.
If I could just tap the ball over to their front court, we'd win. What's the best move here?
Set the ball for Yui.
Use a fake-out shot.
Yui, this one's yours!
Yui's eyes flash with determination as she jumps high into the air...
Whoosh – Yui's powerful spike hits nothing but thin air.
That's quite the powerful whiff, Yui.
How did I miss?
After that, the other team seized the momentum and eventually defeated us.
After the match, Yui just stood there, staring silently at the volleyball rolling across the sand.
It's obvious she's feeling pretty down...
Yui?
My hand position during the spike should have been correct...
Maybe I jumped too soon?
But if I could increase the momentum, perhaps I can maintain kinetic energy while controlling my midair posture better...
Yui finds a stick from somewhere and begins writing complex calculations in the sand.
Yui, the sun's starting to set.
Don't worry, it's just a friendly game!
Yui doesn't seem to hear me, still absorbed in her diagrams and calculations...
Can I get you something to drink?
I'd like an iced coffee.
Sure thing.
My angle is perfect! I start by aiming high toward their back court, then suddenly flip my wrist to hit a clean, straight shot to their undefended front court.
Natsuki lunges desperately toward the ball, but he's just a split second too slow.
When the volleyball hits the sand, the match ends with our victory.
Argh, I just couldn't get there in time!
That was so cool... I had no idea you were faking...
Seeing the disappointed looks on my opponents' faces gives me a little rush of pride.
As I turn to celebrate with my teammates, I suddenly notice something's not right.
Senpai...
... (staring)
Oh, I see...
Sorry, were you waiting for me to set the ball for you?
Now that I think about it, Yui's position was ideal for a spike.
{var:player_nickname}, seriously. As the team leader, you should be more considerate of Yui's feelings.
Hold on a second?! Since when am I the team leader?!
Senpai.
Yui gives my shoulder a little poke with her finger.
Buy me coffee and I'll forgive you.
Eh? Coffee?
Despite what she's saying, Yui doesn't appear angry at all. If anything, she seems almost... happy?
Is she just playing a joke on me...?
Alright. What kind of coffee would you like?
Just a regular iced coffee, thanks.
This is a good opportunity to get some drinks to refresh ourselves after playing. Luckily, there's a vending machine in the nearby parking lot where I easily buy a can of iced coffee.
I might as well buy drinks for everyone else too.
With this in mind, I load all the drinks into a bag. But when I get back to the beach, I'm met with an unexpected situation.
Yui is gone.
Has anyone seen Yui?
Eh? Yui?
You're right. Where did Yui go?
Weird... I can see from one end of this beach to the other, so she shouldn't be hard to find.
At that moment, I suddenly remember what Yui and I talked about earlier.
Did she go into the ocean alone to prove she can swim because I doubted her earlier?!
I'll search along the shoreline!
Good idea! We'll all spread out and search!
If I'm right about this... this could be serious.
We decide to split up and comb the beach, but none of us can find Yui.
There's no way she was pulled out to sea by the waves, right...?
Growing increasingly worried, I follow the shoreline until I reach a rocky area.
The beach gives way to an unbroken stretch of large, jagged rocks that march right out into the ocean.
Phew. Finally, there you are.
Senpai? What's wrong?
Yui doesn't seem to realize what's happened, her eyes clear and curious despite her typical lack of expression.
Thank goodness you're alright... everyone's been worried sick. I need to let them know you're safe.
Wait.
Don't tell them where we are just yet.
Hm?
While I don't know why Yui wants this, I respect her wish and simply message the group: "Found Yui, everything's fine."
I put my phone away, and Yui climbs up onto the rocks to join me.
As she gets closer, I see she's holding several small shimmering white fragments in her palm.
You came all the way out here... for shells.
She must have been so focused on finding seashells that she wandered to this hidden spot without realizing.
Yes, but they're not particularly rare...
Still, I'd like you to have them.
Thank you, Yui. I appreciate it.
There's no need for thanks between us.
Senpai...
Hmm?
Could you stay and talk with me for a bit?
Of course.
She nods, looking satisfied.
The waves crash against the rocks with a soothing sound that's both relaxing and pleasant to the ear.
We sit side by side on the rocks, enjoying the peaceful sea and looking out toward the horizon.
Back in ancient times, I doubt anyone believed the earth beneath them was a sphere.
But there was an ancient civilization that believed the earth was a hemisphere supported on an elephant's back.
And beneath that elephant lurked a turtle even larger than the elephant.
That's quite fascinating, don't you think?
I wonder what it was like for people to first discover they were living on a gigantic sphere.
With how far technology has come, will we ever be truly surprised by a discovery again?
As the sun sinks, its brilliant light traces the outline of Yui's face.
There's something in her expression that I can't quite grasp yet.
You know so much. Is that from your scientist parents' influence?
Yes. They taught me a lot of things when they were still alive.
Wait...?
Yui combs her fingers through her long hair and nods.
They were in a plane crash before I started middle school.
Don't give me that look...
It's all in the past now. I've learned to let it go.
I see... thank you for telling me.
You're incredibly strong, Yui.
It's more like I've gotten so used to being alone that sometimes I feel afraid of how things are now.
I love spending time with all of you, but I don't know how to show you my feelings.
After all, I barely even know how to smile.
Senpai...
What should I do?
I can help you practice smiling.
I can tell when you're happy, you know.
It's never too late to start practicing. I'm sure you'll be smiling naturally in no time.
A natural smile...
What kind of practice should we do?
Well... let me think about it.
To be frank, I don't really know exactly what we should do either.
Perhaps we could start by exercising your facial muscles?
Do you mean the levator labii superioris, orbicularis oris, or masseter muscles?
Or maybe the orbicularis oculi, zygomaticus minor, or depressor anguli oris?
Or rather, the mentalis?
S-sorry, I don't understand any of those terms...
But the human face has about 30 different muscles.
At this point, Yui's eyes suddenly grow wide.
Are you saying everyone practices this advanced mental exercise every day?
That's exhausting... no wonder people often say socializing is complicated...
Let me put it this way...
Look, like this – just use your index fingers to push up the corners of your mouth.
That's a basic smile right there. Wanna try?
Yui puts her index fingers against the corners of her mouth and pushes them up hard. The result looks extremely unnatural and rather funny...
She made a completely mechanical smile.
So Yui really doesn't know how to smile...
Why are you laughing?
Ah, sorry about that.
Watching you give it your all is just too adorable – I couldn't help myself.
Adorable? Me?
Without a word, Yui stares intently at my face.
I hope I didn't upset her...
Ah – so this is where Yui has been hiding!
Following behind her are the rest of our friends. Natsuki is carrying the drinks I bought earlier, and just like that, our group is reunited.
Got busted. Too bad.
Hmm? What was that?
Nothing.
We play among the rocks, all six of us, bathed in the soft afterglow.
Tiny fish swim happily back and forth in the numerous tide pools between the rocks.
As we're all observing the tiny world in the tide pools, Yui suddenly stands up and points to something nearby.
Following her gesture, I spot a strange creature trying to scale a rock, its back covered with writhing tentacles.
That's a hermit crab.
Is THAT what hermit crabs look like?!
Though this is my first time seeing one alive.
I see... hold on, did you just...
Did you just smile?
I can't be completely sure, but I don't think I was imagining it. For just a moment, Yui's lips curved up at the corners.
Eh?
I could be wrong. But from what I saw, you were definitely smiling just now.
Is that so?
...That's great.
Yui says softly, before turning her attention back to the tiny world at her feet.
Her smile still needs practice, but perhaps success isn't too far off.
Until then, I'll enjoy this journey with her.
Really?
Of course.
When you're happy, your eyes crinkle slightly, as if you're looking at something bright.
Your lips might not move, but that's still your own special way of smiling.
That's how I've come to recognize it, at least.
You really are fascinating.
Wait, I think I've heard Yui say something similar before...
What's so fascinating about me?
You always notice things that nobody else does.
I always feel happy when I'm with you.
All these compliments are making me feel a little self-conscious.
Uh, well... um... the ocean looks gorgeous, doesn't it?
Yes, it's stunning.
Wow, the entire sky is painted red now.
Let's watch the sunset together.
We can just stay here until the sun sinks into the sea.
Okay.
It's beautiful.
We turn our gaze toward the distant sunset. If only this moment could stretch on just a little longer...
Ah – so this is where Yui has been hiding!
Following behind her are the rest of our friends, and just like that, our group is finally reunited.
We play among the rocks, all six of us, bathed in the soft afterglow.
Tiny fish swim happily back and forth in the numerous tide pools between the rocks.
Senpai, I need to tell you something.
While the others are absorbed in the tiny world below, Yui speaks in a volume only I can hear.
What is it?
But actually, I've always wanted to share these joys with someone else.
So being able to call everyone – especially you, senpai – my friends makes me incredibly happy.
Playing mahjong or coming to the beach like this... these are things I wouldn't have even imagined doing before.
So, thank you.
For showing me this whole new world.
When Yui finishes speaking, the sun slowly dips below the horizon behind her.
To my eyes, she's smiling.
I should be the one thanking you, Yui.
After all, haven't I too discovered a new world all my own... thanks to her?
I want to see even more expressions on Yui's face in the future.
But for now, I'll keep these thoughts to myself.
As a red glow bathes the entire world, a subtle yet unmistakable smile graces Yui's lips.
The View From Your Side
Yui says this, half to me and half to herself.
Yui... please be okay!
Yes, fascinating indeed.
Climbing onto one of the rocks, I spot a reassuring figure below. It's Yui, crouching on the sand, hidden from everyone's view by the tall rocks.
Which muscle exactly?
To create a perfect smile, I need to precisely control every single muscle's movement.
Hold on, hold on, it's not complicated at all!
I turn toward the sound of the voice and see Hinata standing at the foot of the rocks, waving up at us.
These little fish probably have no idea Earth is a sphere either.
In addition to living in shells, hermit crabs sometimes carry sea anemones on their backs for protection.
And you're very considerate.
Kind to everyone.
I turn toward the sound of the voice and see Hinata standing at the foot of the rocks, waving up at us.
I always thought reading books and brewing coffee brought me joy.
